outlook.statement: While the broad economic consensus is that India will continue to be the fastest growing major economy, there are significant challenges including potentially poor monsoon, limited availability and high prices for energy, re-imposition of tariffs, and new global conflicts. Vehicle manufacturers are positive about the first half but concerns exist about the second half.
Company is expanding its range and presence in the Indian aftermarket which is expected to fuel growth in 2026-27 and beyond.

Impact of US reciprocal tariffs significantly slowed business, but company has mitigated by expanding across other geographies. Initiated testing of novel reusable products to mitigate future tariffs and improve environmental impact, logistics costs, and customer unit economics. Developing niche industrial and railway friction products with initial customer approvals; commercial supplies planned from Q2 2026.

Indian automotive industry expected to maintain steady growth in FY 2026–27, led by sustained demand in SUVs, light commercial vehicles, and improving rural consumption. Expanding vehicle parc, growing freight activity, and increasingly sophisticated customers support aftermarket growth. Global focus on full-vehicle emissions presents opportunities for reusable and zero-emission products. Composite business addresses automotive lightweighting and defense/drone segments. China+1 strategies present domestic and international growth opportunities.

Global economy likely to be extremely volatile with energy availability central (US-Iran conflict, Straits of Hormuz, Ukraine-Russia conflict). World Bank estimated growth could be an over-estimate. Likelihood of re-emergence of US tariffs and Europe's increased protectionism raise headwinds to global trade.

IMF projects 6.5% growth for India in year ahead. Significant El Nino driven weak monsoon and rising consumer debt remove inflation buffer. Exchange rate pressure and domestic inflation likely. Threat of reimposition of US tariffs under Section 301 as early as end of July 2026. European CBAM remains challenge. Bureaucratic and political shortsightedness on ethanol-based fuels poses greatest risk.
